rationale:
Evidence: every trial in iteration 0 left the track (off_track 60/60). Progress was only 0.04 to 0.115, and max_error reached about 0.061, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Each run recorded one line-loss event, so the robot lost the tape early and never recovered. Steering error (rms 0.029) was not the main failure. The likely causes are an aggressive gain/speed combination (kp 3.0 at base_speed 1.7 with a weak kd of 0.05) that overshoots on each bend, and 12 mm sensors spaced 12 mm apart, which blur the line edge.

Changes: (1) Sensors: spacing reduced to 8 mm (x = -0.016 to +0.016) with 8 mm footprints. This gives a sharper, less averaged position estimate, and the outer sensors still see the tape edge. (2) base_speed 1.7 to 1.5: less centrifugal drift and overshoot, while still close to the speed needed to finish. (3) kp 3.0 to 2.0: smaller turn per unit of signal, which reduces oscillation. (4) kd 0.05 to 0.2: more damping of the correction. (5) ki 0.1 to 0.05: less integral lag on bends. (6) mass 0.8 to 0.7 and body_width unchanged: lighter body responds faster to steering. Sensor weights and line_loss are kept so the change in steering response can be isolated.

Expected result: fewer off-track ends, with progress rising toward completion on oval and s-bend. Hypotheses to test: H1, the off-track failures come from overshoot at bends (so lower kp and higher kd should help). H2, the 12 mm sensor blur contributes to the early line loss. The measurements requested will show whether max_error and line_loss_events drop and whether steering_oscillation falls. If the robot now stays on track but finishes too slowly, the next step is to raise base_speed.
